summary: Defines encodings for routing and wavelength assignment information in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks. It follows the information model in RFC 7446 and supports path computation and LSP setup.

eli5.summary: Fiber networks send different colors of light. This defines how to describe which colors are available, so paths can be planned.

questions: what is routing and wavelength assignment
what is a resource block set
subtitle: Compact binary encodings for the optical-node details that wavelength routing and path computation need.

tldr.problem: Planning paths in a Wavelength Switched Optical Network needs detailed information about resource blocks such as wavelength converters and regenerators, and it needs a compact common format to carry it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines protocol-agnostic fields: a Resource Block Set, accessibility, wavelength constraints, pool state, shared-access availability and a Resource Block Information field with typed subfields.
tldr.outcome: Protocol-specific documents can reference these encodings to extend GMPLS routing (OSPF, IS-IS) or to inform a Path Computation Element. The RFC also creates a new IANA registry for the subfield types.

today: RFC 7581 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2015, and no RFC obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the information model in RFC 7446 and the general encodings in RFC 7579.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
A Wavelength Switched Optical Network (WSON) is a Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) network in which switching is done selectively on the center wavelength of an optical signal. RFC 6163 describes a framework for GMPLS and Path Computation Element (PCE) control of a WSON, and RFC 7446 defines an information model of what must be known at various points to compute paths and set up Label Switched Paths (LSPs).

This document supplies efficient encodings of the information the Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) process needs. They are meant to extend GMPLS signaling and routing protocols and could also feed a PCE. Because the encodings are efficient, they allow more accurate analysis of the control-plane load of a GMPLS-controlled WSON. A companion, RFC 7579, encodes information that applies to a wider range of technologies.
sections.eli5: Before you plan a trip you need a map with details. This RFC is the shorthand for writing those details about a light-based network so many tools can read them.

sections.title: Resources, Resource Blocks and the Pool
sections.content:
The encodings are designed to fit the GMPLS routing protocols OSPF (RFC 4203) and IS-IS (RFC 5307) and the PCE Communication Protocol (RFC 5440). Those routing protocols nest sub-TLVs inside TLVs; this document defines the elements used inside such constructs, and the exact nesting is left to the protocol-specific documents.

Five information fields pertain to resources within an optical node: Resource Accessibility, Resource Wavelength Constraints, Resource Block Pool State, Resource Block Shared Access Wavelength Availability and Resource Block Information. Each works with one or more sets of resources rather than a single resource block, which motivates the shared Resource Block Set field.
sections.eli5: A node can hold a shelf of helper boxes. There are five kinds of notes to describe the shelf and which cables reach which box.

sections.title: The Resource Block Set Field
sections.content:
The Resource Block Set (RB Set) field names a group of resource blocks so that shared properties can be described once. It is modeled on the label set concept of RFC 3471.

Its header has an 8-bit Action, a one-bit C (connectivity) flag, 7 reserved bits and a 16-bit Length in bytes. Action 0 is an Inclusive List of RB identifiers. Action 1 is Inclusive Range(s), where each range is two 32-bit identifiers for its start and end. An RB identifier is a 32-bit integer whose scope is local to the node. The C bit is used only in the Resource Accessibility field: 0 means fixed (possibly multicast) connectivity and 1 means potential (switched) connectivity. Reserved bits MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on receipt.

A usage note observes that ranges can be very compact, so resource blocks are best numbered such that status updates can use them.
sections.eli5: It is a way to name a bunch of boxes, either by listing them or by saying from box 5 to box 9.

sections.title: Accessibility and Availability Fields
sections.content:
Resource Accessibility describes how the resource pool relates to the switch: which input ports can reach which sets of resources, and which sets can reach which output ports. These correspond to the PoolInputMatrix and PoolOutputMatrix of RFC 7446. It uses a connectivity bit (0 means fixed, 1 means switched) and pairs of Link Set and RB Set fields, with the link sets encoded as in RFC 7579. The bidirectional direction value is not permitted here.

Resource Wavelength Constraints covers resources, such as wavelength converters, that have limited input or output wavelength ranges. Flag bits I, O and B say whether input constraints, output constraints or one shared constraint field is present. Only (I,O,B) of (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (1,1,0) and (0,0,1) are valid. The constraints are encoded as Label Sets from RFC 7579.

Resource Block Pool State reports how many resources are in use, which changes as LSPs are set up and torn down. Action 0 gives a list of 16-bit counts, one per block, and Action 1 gives a bitmap with 0 for available and 1 for in use. The bitmap is a multiple of 4 bytes and is padded.

Shared Access Wavelength Availability is used when blocks are reached through a shared fiber, and lists the wavelengths currently available on the input fiber, output fiber or both.
sections.eli5: These notes say which cables reach which boxes, which colors a box can use, how many boxes are busy, and which colors are free on a shared cable.

sections.title: The Resource Block Information Field
sections.content:
The ResourceBlockInfo field conveys relatively static facts about resource blocks: their optical interface classes, acceptable client signals, input bit rate, and processing capabilities such as the number of resources in a block, regeneration, performance monitoring and vendor-specific features. It starts with an RB Set, then I, O and B bits for shared fibers, then zero or more optional subfields.

Each subfield has a 16-bit Type and 16-bit Length (in bytes, without padding), and is padded to 4-byte alignment. Unrecognized types are not processed, and if a type appears several times only the first SHOULD be processed. The initial types are 1 (Optical Interface Class List), 2 (Acceptable Client Signal List), 3 (Input Bit Rate List) and 4 (Processing Capability List).

The Acceptable Client Signal List holds a count and a list of G-PIDs, and the Input Bit Rate List must have one rate per G-PID, in IEEE 754 floating point format. The Processing Capability List uses a Processing Cap ID: 1 Regeneration, 2 Fault and performance monitoring, 3 Vendor-specific. A regenerator is typed 1R, 2R or 3R and is either a Fixed Regeneration Point or in Selective Regeneration Pools; the latter value needs an additional specification before it can be used.

For IANA, the RFC creates the "GMPLS Routing Parameters for WSON" registry, used only in routing and not in signaling. Its subregistry for subfield types is maintained via Standards Action, with 0 reserved and 5 through 65535 unassigned.
sections.eli5: Each helper box gets a label with optional stickers: which light types it can take, which signals it accepts, how fast, and what extra jobs it does.

sections.title: Optical Interface Class Encoding
sections.content:
The Optical Interface Class List has I and O flags: input only, output only or both (0 and 0 is invalid). Each class is a 64-bit value preceded by a header with an S (Standard) bit and an OI Code Points field. S=0 identifies non-ITU code points, where only 0 (reserved) is defined. S=1 identifies ITU application codes: 1 for G.698.1, 2 for G.698.2, 3 for G.959.1 and 4 for G.695.

For each ITU recommendation the RFC maps the letters of the application code string, such as the channel spacing, haul length, fiber type and wavelength band, into bit fields of the 64-bit class, with a flag for an optional FEC suffix. For G.698.1 and G.698.2 the last 32 bits are reserved and set to zero. Values not listed are not allowed. The RFC does not restate the ITU definitions; it points to the ITU documents for them.
sections.eli5: Optical gear has a model code. This turns that code into a fixed-size number so computers can compare it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document defines protocol-independent encodings and states that it does not introduce any security issues. Other documents that use the encodings in protocol extensions need to consider the risks of inspection, interception, modification or spoofing of this information and describe the security measures needed. A general discussion of security in GMPLS networks is in RFC 5920.
sections.eli5: This RFC only writes the shorthand. Whoever sends the notes must still keep them safe from snooping or tampering.

sections.title: Encoding Examples
sections.content: Appendix A gives worked examples: a Wavelength Converter Accessibility field, a Wavelength Conversion Range field, and an optical-electrical-optical (OEO) switch with DWDM optics. The first illustrates a wavelength converter pool architecture known as "shared per fiber", described by input and output pool matrices.
sections.eli5: The back of the RFC shows filled-in examples, like a sample form, so you can see how the shorthand looks in real use.

fields.name: Action
fields.desc: 0 is an Inclusive List; 1 is Inclusive Range(s).

fields.name: C
fields.desc: 0 fixed, 1 switched connectivity; used in Resource Accessibility.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: MUST be zero when sent and ignored on receipt.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length of the field in bytes.

fields.name: RB Identifier 1
fields.desc: 32-bit identifier local to the node; more follow.

items.label: Acceptable Client Signal List
items.desc: G-PIDs that are accepted as input.

items.label: Input Bit Rate List
items.desc: One bit rate per listed G-PID.
